name: @projexlight/connector-snowflake
summary: Bidirectional Snowflake connector for ProjexCloud: install per-tenant + bind ProjexCloud tables to Snowflake target tables, run scheduled sync runs (push, pull, or merge), query Snowflake from the lakehouse federation layer. Customer credentials vault-stored; per-bind sync logs let the customer + ProjexCloud reconcile cost + freshness without sharing the warehouse password.

events.name: connector-snowflake.install.created.v1
events.description: Customer installed the connector + provided credentials.

events.name: connector-snowflake.binding.created.v1
events.description: Table-to-table binding registered (ProjexCloud table ↔ Snowflake table).

events.name: connector-snowflake.sync.completed.v1
events.description: Sync run finished; carries rows_pushed, rows_pulled, duration_ms.

events.name: connector-snowflake.sync.failed.v1
events.description: Sync run failed; carries error class + retry plan.

events.name: connector-snowflake.query.served.v1
events.description: Federation query routed to Snowflake; logged for cost attribution.

models.description: Per-tenant install: account_url, warehouse, database, role, credentials_vault_ref.
Per-binding row: source_table, target_table, sync_mode (push / pull / merge), schedule.
Per-run row: binding_id, started_at, finished_at, rows_in, rows_out, status.
Per-federated-query row: query_hash, rows_returned, duration_ms, snowflake_warehouse_seconds.

hooks.name: installConnector
hooks.description: Register a tenant's Snowflake credentials (vault-wrapped) + validate the connection.

hooks.name: registerBinding
hooks.description: Wire a source (ProjexCloud) table to a target (Snowflake) table with a sync mode + schedule.

hooks.name: runSyncNow
hooks.description: Force-run a sync regardless of schedule. Useful after the customer fixes a Snowflake side issue.

hooks.name: startScheduler
hooks.description: Background worker that drives scheduled sync runs. Safe to leave running in dev.

hooks.name: queryFederated
hooks.description: Run a Snowflake query as part of an sdk-analytics federation. Logged for cost attribution.

scenarios.title: Customer installs Snowflake connector via tenant-admin Connectors page
scenarios.when_to_use: First-time setup. Customer provides account URL + service-user credentials; we validate the connection + store credentials vault-wrapped.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Install row written; credentials stored in sdk-vault under a fresh key; emits connector-snowflake.install.created.v1. Tenant admin sees the install in their Connectors page with a green health dot.

scenarios.title: Push canonical invoices to a Snowflake fact table
scenarios.when_to_use: Customer wants billing data in their Snowflake account for BI tools. Bind ProjexCloud billing.invoice → snowflake FACT_INVOICE every hour.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Binding row written + scheduler picks up the cadence. Hourly sync runs land in connector_snowflake.sync_run with row counts + duration. Customer's BI dashboards refresh on the same cadence.

scenarios.title: Customer fixed a Snowflake permission issue; force-resync now
scenarios.when_to_use: Sync was failing because of a permission gap; customer fixed it; we don't want to wait for the next scheduled tick.
scenarios.example_code:
import { runSyncNow } from '@projexlight/connector-snowflake';
const { sync_run_id } = await runSyncNow({ binding_id });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Immediate sync run; result lands in sync_run with the new status. Emits .sync.completed.v1 or .sync.failed.v1.

scenarios.title: sdk-analytics federation routes a query to Snowflake
scenarios.when_to_use: Federated analytics query spans both Iceberg lakehouse + Snowflake; this connector executes the Snowflake leg.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns rows + warehouse_seconds. The latter is the cost attribution unit — both ProjexCloud + the customer can reconcile Snowflake bills against actual usage.

scenarios.title: Tenant offboards → drop the install + revoke credentials
scenarios.when_to_use: Reactive worker on tenant.offboarded.v1 — credentials shredded; sync history retained per the tenant's retention policy for dispute resolution.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Vault key for the credential blob shredded — making the credentials undecryptable. Sync history rows retained but with credentials_vault_ref tombstoned.

compliance_posture.notes: Customer credentials always vault-wrapped — we never log raw credentials. EU-residency tenants pin sync_mode + warehouse region to keep data in-jurisdiction. Snowflake itself is SOC2-attested; our use of it inherits the chain when customer chooses a region-appropriate account.

pricing_skus.unit_description: per federated query (Snowflake warehouse-seconds billed passthrough)
